disclaimer: Sowing windows are educational planning estimates. A USDA hardiness zone describes average extreme winter cold; it is not a vegetable planting forecast. Local temperature, microclimate, unusual weather, variety, seed-packet directions, and extension guidance may shift the best date.

crops.label: Leaf lettuce
crops.note: Choose bolt-resistant varieties as conditions warm and use protected starts during peak heat.

crops.label: Arugula
crops.note: Best quality comes from cool growing conditions.

crops.label: Cilantro
crops.note: Cilantro bolts quickly in sustained heat, so use short succession intervals in its cool window.

crops.label: Parsley
crops.note: Germination is naturally slow; keep the seed surface evenly moist.

crops.label: Dill
crops.note: Direct sow because dill dislikes root disturbance.

crops.label: Kale
crops.note: Protected starts can stage the next crop while outdoor conditions remain hot.

crops.label: Mustard greens
crops.note: Mustard grows quickly; harvest young leaves or allow selected plants to mature.

crops.label: Mizuna
crops.note: A useful fast succession crop for cool-season tower pockets.

crops.label: Bok choy
crops.note: Heat and stress can trigger bolting, so favor the cool window.

crops.label: Swiss chard
crops.note: One of the most adaptable HydroPip greens across changing seasons.

crops.label: Basil
crops.note: Wait for warm conditions and pinch growing tips to delay flowering.

crops.label: Malabar spinach
crops.note: A heat-tolerant vine that needs separate support and benefits from a protected start.

crops.label: Leaf amaranth
crops.note: A strong warm-season leafy option; avoid crowding mature plants.

crops.label: Oregano
crops.note: Slow early growth makes a protected start easier to manage.

crops.label: Thyme
crops.note: Tiny, slow seedlings are easier to establish in a protected cell.

crops.label: Purslane
crops.note: A heat-tolerant crop for the hottest part of the season.

crops.label: Green beans
crops.note: Direct sow and use compact bush varieties or provide separate support for pole beans; avoid crowding tower pockets.

crops.label: Compact pepper
crops.note: Use a protected start and provide plant support; reserve only selected tower pockets for fruiting plants.

crops.label: Supported cherry tomato
crops.note: Use a protected start, dedicated support, pruning, and a limited number of tower pockets.

crops.label: Strawberry
crops.note: Crowns or plugs are usually more practical than seed for a first HydroPip strawberry crop.
